forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Uttlesford expects to use reserves from 2026/27 as funding falls
news_drafts.lead: Uttlesford achieved a £0.854m underspend in 2025/26 without drawing on reserves, but the council now expects to use its reserves from 2026/27 onwards to cover projected deficits caused by reduced government funding following the Fair Funding Review. The council holds sufficient reserves to cover these deficits and is pursuing efficiency savings through its Blueprint 2.0 programme, targeting £900,000 in 2026/27 and £2.5m by 2030/31. However, the Audit and Standards Committee heard that 33 audit recommendations now remain overdue, including one critical priority item. Housing has been a persistent area of concern, with the audit identifying control weaknesses in an £8.6m maintenance contract, including undocumented payment discrepancies, and unresolved recommendations on debt recovery and project management that date back over a year.

findings.headline: KPMG notes the Constitution is dated September 2023 with no expected review date, and recommends a version number and review date on policies.
findings.detail: The paper records a recommendation on keeping policies and the Constitution up to date, including adding version numbers, scheduled review dates and annual reviews. It also records that the Head of Internal Audit reviews fraud risk and reports to the Audit and Standards Committee and the s151 officer.
findings.matters: A governance recommendation on policy review dates is a routine-looking item that other councils' audit committees may be asked to check in their own documents.
findings.quote: We however noted that this is dated September 2023 with no expected review date.

findings.headline: Government announced on 7 September 2026 a review of the local government reorganisation programme, with some proposals withdrawn and others paused.
findings.detail: The paper says the timetable and scope of reorganisation remain subject to further Government decisions. It also notes KPMG's review of the Council's LGR preparations covers activity only up to 31 March 2026.
findings.matters: The timetable for reorganisation determines how long councils must plan on their current reserves and savings, which is the basis for the MTFP assumptions a lender would examine.
findings.quote: On 7 September 2026, the Government announced a review of the local government reorganisation programme

findings.headline: Axis Europe's housing management contract was terminated six months after it began, and the service was insourced.
findings.detail: The paper says the Axis Europe contract began on 1 April 2025 and was terminated after several performance issues. Cabinet considered in-house options in December and the service was then insourced. Contractual disputes with both UNSL and Axis Europe are ongoing and under review by KPMG.
findings.matters: A contract terminated within six months, followed by insourcing and open disputes, is an outsourcing reversal that other councils with similar housing contracts would want to compare.
findings.quote: The Axis Europe contract was subsequently terminated six months after commencement because of several performance issues.

findings.headline: KPMG identifies no significant weaknesses in the value for money arrangements, with no significant risks identified in financial sustainability, governance or economy, efficiency and effectiveness.
findings.detail: The paper concludes that no significant risks were identified in any of the three value for money criteria. It notes the work on these criteria is substantially complete.
findings.matters: A clean value for money conclusion alongside a reserves-dependent MTFP is the combination a finance director at another council would want to see explained.
findings.quote: We identified no significant weaknesses in respect of the arrangements

findings.headline: Head of Internal Audit opinion is Moderate Assurance for 2025-26, against Limited assurance for 2024-25, with 7 control deficiencies in the Annual Governance Statement against 5.
findings.detail: The paper's governance table shows the opinion moved up one level and the number of control deficiencies reported in the Annual Governance Statement rose from 5 to 7.
findings.matters: An audit opinion that has moved up a grade is a change that a finance director elsewhere can compare with their own internal audit position, even with more deficiencies reported.
findings.quote: Head of Internal Audit Opinion Moderate Assurance Limited assurance
